rules: Each finding has its own written search of every PubMed record in Europe PMC (titles and abstracts); all reviews, randomised trials and guidelines it found were downloaded.
Left out animal studies (MeSH tags, or the title when there are none) and retracted papers.
A review counts for a finding when the finding's search found it and the finding's words are in its title.

Reviews: meta-analyses or systematic reviews of any design, because most of what is known about habits like walking, sleep or sauna comes from studies that follow people over years, as well as from trials. Chosen: the three newest meta-analyses (systematic reviews only if fewer than three), plus the most comprehensive one (most studies pooled, read from the abstract). Citations are shown but do not choose.
Newer large trials: randomised trials of at least 1,000 people (read from the abstract) from the year of the newest chosen review on, which those reviews may not include.

Screening: each eligible review's title and abstract was read against the finding's question (who, which habit or exposure, compared with what, what was measured) by Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only. Only reviews that answer it can be chosen; the others are listed with the reason. The decisions are kept in the repository and have not yet been checked by a clinician.
Overlap between the chosen reviews isn't shown: they mostly pool cohort studies, which aren't downloaded, so shared studies can't be counted reliably.

left.title: The Clinical Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Patients with Insomnia and Depression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
left.reason: Pools CBT-I vs no treatment on insomnia scales, but only in people whose insomnia comes with depression.

left.title: Non-pharmacological treatment for insomnia following acquired brain injury: A systematic review
left.reason: Reviews non-drug insomnia treatments including CBT, but only in adults after brain injury or stroke.

left.title: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials Evaluating the Evidence Base of Melatonin, Light Exposure, Exercise, and Complementary and Alternative Medicine for Patients with Insomnia Disorder
left.reason: The network meta-analysis is about melatonin, light, exercise and CAM, with CBT-I only as a reference treatment.

left.title: Changes in dysfunctional beliefs about sleep after cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia: A systematic literature review and meta-analysis
left.reason: CBT-I trials against controls, but the outcome is dysfunctional beliefs about sleep, not sleep onset, waking, efficiency or severity.

left.title: Economic evaluation of cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) for improving health outcomes in adult populations: A systematic review
left.reason: Economic evaluations of CBT-I, so the outcome is cost-effectiveness rather than sleep.

left.title: The efficacy of cognitive and behavior therapies for insomnia on daytime symptoms: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
left.reason: CBT-I in insomnia, but the outcomes are daytime symptoms, not sleep onset, waking, efficiency or severity.

left.title: Comparison between acupuncture and cognitive behavioral therapy for primary insomnia: A protocol for systematic review and network meta-analysis
left.reason: This is a protocol only, so no studies have been reviewed or pooled yet, although the planned PICO is close.

left.title: Psychosocial intervention for discontinuing benzodiazepine hypnotics in patients with chronic insomnia: A systematic review and meta-analysis
left.reason: Narrower group: chronic insomnia patients stopping benzodiazepines; CBT-I plus tapering against tapering alone, with insomnia symptoms.

left.title: Insomnia and Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in Elderly People: A Systematic Review
left.reason: Technology-delivered CBT-I in older adults only, with outcomes like disability and quality of life, not sleep measures.

left.title: Economic evaluation of cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) for improving health outcomes in adult population: a systematic review protocol
left.reason: Protocol for a review of CBT-I costs, with no sleep outcomes and no studies reviewed yet.

left.title: Insomnia and mortality: A meta-analysis
left.reason: Looks at the link between insomnia and death, not at CBT-I treatment.

left.title: Efficacy of cognitive behavioral therapy in children and adolescents with insomnia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
left.reason: CBT-I with sleep onset and efficiency outcomes, but in children and adolescents rather than adults.

left.title: Digitally-delivered cognitive-behavioural therapy for youth insomnia: A systematic review
left.reason: Digital CBT-I with sleep outcomes, but the population is young people and adolescents, not adults.

left.title: Current Treatment of Comorbid Insomnia and Obstructive Sleep Apnea With CBTI and PAP-Therapy: A Systematic Review
left.reason: Limited to insomnia with sleep apnea, and CBT-I is mostly combined with PAP therapy.

left.title: The cognitive treatment components and therapies of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia: A systematic review
left.reason: It reviews only the cognitive components of CBT-I, not the full programme, and comparators are not stated.

left.title: The effectiveness of behavioural and cognitive behavioural therapies for insomnia on depressive and fatigue symptoms: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
left.reason: Looks at CBT-I effects on depression and fatigue symptoms, not on sleep onset, wake time, efficiency or insomnia severity.

left.title: Effect of insomnia treatments on depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis
left.reason: Looks at insomnia treatments in people with depression, with depression as the outcome rather than sleep.

left.title: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) to treat depression: A systematic review
left.reason: Reviews CBT-I as a treatment for depression, with depression outcomes rather than sleep outcomes.

left.title: Does cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia improve cognitive performance? A systematic review and narrative synthesis
left.reason: Looks at CBT-I effects on cognitive performance, not on sleep onset, wake time, efficiency or insomnia severity.

left.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of cognitive behavior therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) in cancer survivors
left.reason: RCTs of CBT-I versus control with SE, SOL, WASO and ISI, but limited to people with cancer.

left.title: Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (ICBT-i) Improves Comorbid Anxiety and Depression-A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
left.reason: The outcomes are anxiety and depression, not sleep onset, wake time, sleep efficiency or insomnia severity.

left.title: Cognitive and behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) in psychiatric populations: a systematic review
left.reason: CBT-I reviewed only in psychiatric comorbid groups; comparators and specific sleep outcomes are not stated.

left.title: Sleeping well with cancer: a systematic review of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia in cancer patients
left.reason: CBT-I with subjective sleep outcomes, including controlled studies, but limited to people with cancer.

left.title: Adherence to cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia: a systematic review
left.reason: The review covers adherence to CBT-I, not its effect against a control on sleep outcomes.

left.title: Yoga as Treatment for Insomnia Among Cancer Patients and Survivors: A Systematic Review
left.reason: The intervention is yoga, not CBT-I.

left.title: Comparative effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia: a systematic review
left.reason: CBT-I is compared with medication, not with waiting list, sleep advice, sham or usual care.

left.title: Meta-analytic review of the impact of cognitive-behavior therapy for insomnia on concomitant anxiety
left.reason: The outcome is anxiety, not sleep onset, wake time, sleep efficiency or insomnia severity.

left.title: [Insomnias. II. Pharmacological and psychotherapeutic treatment options]
left.reason: This is a narrative overview of drug and psychological treatments, not a systematic review of CBT-I versus control.

left.title: The association between sleep variability and cognitive function: A systematic review and meta analysis
left.reason: The exposure (sleep variability) matches, but the outcome is cognitive function, not death or cardiometabolic health.

left.title: Sleep timing and health indicators in children and adolescents: a systematic review
left.reason: Covers children and adolescents and looks at sleep timing rather than regularity, mostly with non-cardiometabolic outcomes.

left.title: Associations between social jetlag and mental health in young people: A systematic review
left.reason: Covers young people and social jetlag, with mental health outcomes rather than death or cardiometabolic health.
